title: $71,000 a Year Is How Much an Hour? (2026)
metaDescription: $71,000 a year is $34.13/hour at 40 hrs/week — $1,365.38 weekly, $5,917 monthly. Full 2026 breakdown with a federal take-home estimate.

hero.lede: Based on a 40-hour week worked 52 weeks a year (2,080 hours). Below: every pay-period equivalent, the rate at other workweeks, a 2026 federal take-home estimate, and how $71,000 compares with the U.S. median.

shortAnswer.heading: How much is $71,000 a year per hour?
shortAnswer.html: $71,000 a year is $34.13 an hour at 40 hours a week, 52 weeks a year (2,080 hours). That's $273.08 a day, $1,365.38 a week, $2,730.77 biweekly, and $5,916.67 a month — all gross. After estimated federal income tax and FICA, a single filer keeps about $58,779 a year, roughly $4,898 a month.

sections.title: What $71,000 looks like per paycheck.
sections.note: All figures are gross (pre-tax). See the take-home table below for the federal-only estimate after taxes.

sections.title: Where $71,000 stands in 2026.
paragraphs: At 40 hours a week, $71,000 a year is $34.13 an hour. That is the offer-letter number, not the bank-deposit number: gross pay lands at $2,730.77 per biweekly check, and what actually arrives depends on taxes and benefits withheld.

For context, the median full-time U.S. worker earns $1,251 a week per the BLS (BLS, Q2 2026) — about $65,052 a year — so this salary runs roughly 9% ahead of the middle of the distribution. A useful rule of thumb at this level: every extra $1 of hourly pay is worth about $2,080 a year at full time, so small raises compound faster than they feel.

sections.title: The hourly rate depends on your hours.
sections.note: Salaried roles rarely pay overtime — at 45 hours a week the same $71,000 effectively pays $30.34 per hour worked.

sections.title: From $71,000 gross to take-home.
sections.note: Single filer, standard deduction, no state/local income tax, no credits or pre-tax benefits. Your actual paycheck will differ.

sections.title: Why the 22% bracket doesn't mean 22% tax.
paragraphs: Only $54,900 of this salary is actually taxable federally once the 2026 standard deduction of $16,100 is applied. Federal income tax totals $6,790 — a 9.6% effective rate even though the marginal bracket is 22% — and employee FICA adds $5,432.

After those federal deductions, take-home is roughly $58,779 a year — $2,260.71 per biweekly paycheck. On a 50/30/20 plan that budget supports about $2,449/month of essentials, $1,469/month of discretionary spending, and $980/month toward savings, before any state income tax.

faq.q: How much is $71,000 a year per hour?
faq.a: $71,000 a year is $34.13 an hour at 40 hours a week (2,080 hours a year). At 37.5 hours a week it rises to $36.41 an hour, and if you actually work 45-hour weeks it averages $30.34 per hour worked.

faq.q: How much is $71,000 a year biweekly?
faq.a: Gross biweekly pay on $71,000 is $2,730.77 ($71,000 ÷ 26 pay periods). After estimated federal income tax and FICA for a single filer, roughly $2,260.71 per check remains — before state taxes and benefits.

faq.q: How much is $71,000 a year after taxes?
faq.a: Using 2026 federal brackets and the $16,100 standard deduction, a single filer earning $71,000 pays about $6,790 in federal income tax and $5,432 in FICA, keeping roughly $58,779 a year ($4,898.21 a month). This is a federal-only estimate — state and local taxes reduce it further.

$71,000 is about 9% above the U.S. median full-time salary of roughly $65,052 (BLS, Q2 2026: $1,251/week). Whether it is "good" depends heavily on your metro's cost of living, household size, and debt load — the same salary goes much further in a low-cost region than in an expensive coastal city.

faq.q: What tax bracket is $71,000 in for 2026?
faq.a: After the $16,100 standard deduction, $71,000 leaves $54,900 of taxable income, which puts a single filer in the 22% marginal bracket for 2026. Only income above each threshold is taxed at the higher rate, so the effective federal rate is just 9.6%.

methodology: Conversions are straight arithmetic on gross salary: $71,000 ÷ 2,080 hours (40 × 52) for hourly, ÷ 260 workdays for daily, ÷ 52, 26, 24 and 12 for the pay-period figures. No taxes are applied to those rows.

The take-home estimate uses 2026 federal brackets for a single filer with the $16,100 standard deduction, plus employee FICA (6.2% Social Security + 1.45% Medicare). It excludes state/local income tax, credits, and pre-tax benefits such as 401(k) or health premiums — so real paychecks will differ.
The median comparison uses BLS median usual weekly earnings for full-time wage and salary workers: $1,251/week (BLS, Q2 2026).
Educational estimates only — not tax, legal, or financial advice.
